# Verdict replay fixtures (S1 history-replay ratchet)

Real receipts from both Macs, copied read-only on 2026-11-02 (~00:17Z):

| File | Source |
|---|---|
| `m4-*.log` | MacBook Pro M4: `~/.local/share/brainlayer/logs/{backup-daily,jsonl-backup,maintenance}.log` |
| `m1-*.log` | M1 Pro (`ssh m1 'cat ~/.local/share/brainlayer/logs/<file>'`) |

Kept: JSON rows whose `attempted_at` / `ts` / `at` falls in 2026-10-12 .. 2026-11-02 (one week of
lookback before the 2026-10-19 replay start). Changed: the `resumable_upload` key is dropped (it holds a
resumable-upload capability URL) and home directories are renamed (`/Users/m4-user`, `/Users/m1-user`).
Drive file ids, md5s and sizes are kept. Rows are re-serialized with sorted keys; nothing else is edited.

`oracle.json` is generated by `build_oracle.py` (`python3 -I tests/fixtures/verdict_replay/build_oracle.py
tests/fixtures/verdict_replay`). It is deliberately separate code from `brainlayer.health_verdict`: plain
dict walking, no BrainLayer imports. It shares the documented evidence rules, not the parser:

- local copy verified: `local_verified` with `local_integrity == "ok"`, or a Drive-verified upload (which
  proves the snapshot it came from); value time = `snapshot_created_at`, else the artifact date at 00:00Z;
- Drive copy verified: `uploaded` and `verified`, no md5 mismatch or verification error;
- transcripts verified: `jsonl-backup.log` rows with `verified` and status `uploaded`/`no-op`/`created`;
- Drive auth: `DriveCredentialError` / "Drive access expired" gives `consent_needed`; a verified upload gives `ok`.

Every event carries `known_from = attempted_at` and `known_by = attempted_at + 8h`, because receipts record
when an invocation started, not when it wrote the row, and carry no completion field. Eight hours is an
upper bound, not an estimate: it is the longest default run limit of the two writers (backup-daily
`DEFAULT_BACKUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, 8 h; the jsonl-backup wrapper, 2 h), and a run killed at its limit
writes no verified row. An hour where the state differs between those bounds is `unknown` and is not
asserted, and so is an hour with no backup evidence at all. The oracle's age limits are its own
constants (`ORACLE_LIMITS_H` in the test), not production's `Thresholds`. Hours the logs say nothing about (ingest, stores, search, disk,
embedding) are not replayed at all.
